summary: Ingress prioritizer starvation causes intermittent 5xx waves and serving-runtime thread spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Multiple customers (notably CortexAI Inc) experienced repeated 5xx responses from the Redwood API between 2026-03-13T15:10Z and 2026-03-13T16:25Z. API Gateway returned 502/503/504 waves when upstream serving-runtime became unresponsive or closed connections. Impact: degraded streaming sessions (socket resets), elevated tail latency for short-text generation, and increased error-rate for dedicated tenants in us-east-1.

Impact:
- Affected ~12 dedicated tenants (priority workloads), CortexAI observed ~40% failure rate on streaming sessions for 15 minutes.
- API error budget at risk for several enterprise customers.

Environment:
- prod (us-east-1) cluster: ingress-shard-7, runtime-pool-dedicated-3
- Autoscaler group: asg-serving-dedicated-us-east-3

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Replay customer traffic shape: sustained small streaming sessions from ~250 concurrent clients with bursty ingress pattern (many short-lived connections).
2) Observe API gateway metrics for 5xx and upstream latency.
3) Correlate with runtime thread/worker CPU and threadpool queues.

Observed telemetry and logs:
- api-gateway: 502 spikes with increased upstream EOF count and connection reset rate (+600% compared to baseline).
- edge-ingress: large increase in per-tenant priority-queue depth; head-of-line blocking observed.
- serving-runtime: threadpool contention spikes; per-worker thread count inflated, context-switch rate up ~3x. GPU utilization remained nominal but runtime reported blocked worker threads waiting on ingress IO.
- autoscaler: triggered scale up events while ingress queues were still saturated, leading to allocation churn and brief GPU allocation failures (transient OOM warnings).

Initial hypothesis:
The edge ingress prioritizer allowed one or a few high-throughput tenants to saturate the prioritized ingress queue while deprioritizing other tenant work. Head-of-line blocking stalled multi-tenant IO to runtimes, which caused runtimes to accumulate blocked threads and trigger autoscaler churn. API Gateway then returned 502/503 when it could not get timely responses from upstream.

Temporary mitigation applied (by on-call):
- Lowered per-tenant concurrency cap for affected dedicated pool (reduced from 300 -> 120 concurrent streaming sessions).
- Enabled stricter per-tenant backpressure at edge (throttle_policy=aggressive) to prevent priority queue monopolization.
- Manually paused a rolling rollout of ingress-priority v2 that had been deployed in shard 7 at 14:50Z.

Next steps (pending):
- Engineering to roll a patch to ingress-priority that fixes head-of-line locking by switching to segmented queues and adding a fair-dequeue algorithm. PR drafted and linked.
- Adjust autoscaler heuristics to consider per-worker IO queue depth before scaling.
- Run targeted load tests with replay harness simulating CortexAI traffic pattern.
- Customer CS outreach scheduled to explain root cause and mitigations.

Attachments/links: dashboards and sample logs in related confluence pages above.

investigation_notes: Traces show a strong correlation between ingress priority queue depth and upstream EOF counts. tcpdump on edge showed many SYN/FIN cycles consistent with short-lived connection churn. Runtimes were not OOMing on GPU memory but thread stacks show blocked reads waiting on epoll. Autoscaler saw high queue depth and initiated scale-up which briefly increased allocation churn and ephemeral allocation failures; this amplified the 5xx rate. No evidence of kernel-level network failures or cloud provider network incidents at that time.
root_cause: Ingress prioritizer allowed head-of-line monopolization by bursty tenants. This produced IO starvation for other tenant streams leading to blocked runtime threads and autoscaler-induced allocation churn, manifesting as 502/503/504 errors from API Gateway.
resolution: Workaround applied: reduced per-tenant concurrency and enabled aggressive backpressure at ingress (2026-03-13 15:30Z). Permanent fix planned: merge and roll out ingress-priority PR that introduces segmented queues + fair-dequeue algorithm, and update autoscaler to consider IO queue depth before scaling. Target hotfix roll-forward to prod 2026-03-17 after successful canary. Notify customers and schedule follow-up postmortem.
